newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: De Boer turnover rose over 25 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: De Boer turnover rose over 25 pct in 1996.

text.p: Supermarkets group De Boer Winkelbedrijven NV said its net turnover rose more than 25 percent to 2.1 billion guilders in 1996.

De Boer said the increased sales figure was due in part to the acquisition of all shares in wholesaler Karsten Groothandel Holding and further growth in the number of franchise operators for its De Boer, Trekpleister and Mitra store formulas.
The company said it would publish full 1996 results on March 11.
Supermarkets chain De Boer and De Jong saw their combined turnover rise six percent in 1996, including turnover booked by franchise operators.

The Dutch supermarkets sector as a whole saw its turnover rise by some three percent last year, so the combined market share of De Boer and De Jong rose to 3.9 percent from 3.8 percent, the company added.
The company's drug store chain Trekpleister achieved a market share of eight percent while its alcoholic drinks retail chain Mitra had a market share of seven percent.
De Boer announced plans in October for a merger with unlisted wholesaler Unigro NV in a move which would create a group with sales of over six billion guilders a year.
